mentioned.quote: Without any safeguards, we recognize that advanced AI models could lower the barrier to entry for bad actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (“CBRN”) or cyber weapons

threshold.quote: Engaging in conduct with no meaningful human oversight, intervention, or supervision that is either a cyberattack or, if the conduct had been committed by a human, would constitute the crime of murder, assault, extortion, or theft, including theft by false pretense.
threshold.note: Ambiguous: item (B) of the Catastrophic Risk definition in footnote 1 (p.1: more than 50 people or $1 billion), adopted as scope on p.1 and used on p.3 ('we particularly focus on requests that pose a Catastrophic Risk') to trigger heightened safeguards.

response.note: p.3 'apply heightened safeguards' names none; p.6 'xAI currently relies on our basic refusal policy to prevent misuse for cyber attacks' and 'still working on identifying enforceable critical steps' are practice and unfinished work; p.6 input and output filters are unconditional practice (E1); p.10 pre-deployment review is review only; the p.6 acceptance criterion covers biology and chemistry only.

acc_decider.note: Only risk owners with 'responsibility for proactively mitigating identified risks', periodic audits and incident monitoring (p.9); none is said to decide whether a threshold is reached, whether the response is adequate, or whether to deploy.

acc_external.note: External involvement is not committed: p.2 'works with ... private testing firms' describes bottleneck identification; p.5-6 independent third-party assessments are past findings; p.8 'we may also provide vetted and qualified external red teams ... unredacted versions' is hedged.

acc_unmet.note: No statement of what happens if a required response is unmet; p.9 steps are all 'may' and cover imminent catastrophic events; p.8 employee reporting of nonadherence goes to no named body; p.9 audits have no stated consequence.
